content.text:
**Partly. I should have checked the narrower options first.** GitHub exposes an on/off switch for AI detection, but no documented controls for its prompt, sensitivity, or “ignore SHA-256 hashes” rules. [GitHub API docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos)

There are two practical alternatives:

- **Path exclusions:** `.github/secret_scanning.yml` can exclude transcript files. However, those exclusions also suppress standard secret alerts and push protection for those files, potentially hiding real leaked keys. [Exclusion docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-secrets/customize-leak-detection/exclude-folders-and-files)
- **Targeted automatic dismissal:** Re-enable AI detection and add automation that closes only password alerts whose surrounding content proves they are package hashes or session identifiers. Unrecognized password findings and provider-token alerts stay open. GitHub supports closing alerts through its API. [Alert API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning)

**I recommend targeted dismissal for this repo.** All the alerts we checked came from checkpoint transcripts, but excluding transcripts entirely would remove useful coverage. This would customize alert handling rather than GitHub’s detector, so alerts may briefly appear before dismissal.

AI detection is still disabled; I haven’t changed anything further.
